reply:
Good question — real-time notifications change the picture slightly but don't break this architecture. Since your containers are already behind an ALB, you have two clean paths:

1. **Managed approach (recommended):** Add Amazon SNS + AWS Lambda fan-out to push notifications (email/push), and use ElastiCache Redis Pub/Sub for in-app live updates. Your existing Redis instance handles this with a size bump.

2. **WebSocket approach:** Add an ALB-native WebSocket endpoint on the same Fargate service, using Redis Pub/Sub to fan out messages across tasks.

Both keep the relational core untouched. I'd start with option 1 — it's cheaper and you can add WebSockets later if you need presence/cursors.

proposed_changes.description: Add Amazon SNS for notification fan-out
proposed_changes.detail: SNS topics for email and push notifications; Lambda subscribes to domain events from the API.
Consumes SNS events and delivers via SES (email) and FCM/APNs (push). Pay-per-use, ~$1-3/month at your volume.
Needed for Redis Pub/Sub headroom once live updates are enabled. Adds ~$20/month.
